Error.description: Every failure body is `{"error": "..."}`. A few routes add fields: publish adds `code` and `requires_ack` when a payment form has no products.

FormStats.description: One row per form: the form's own mode, its entry count (responses for a response form, sales for a payment form) and its money figures.

FormWrite.description: Form fields to create or change. `config` is the builder document (blocks); sending it replaces the stored config.

scopes.description: readonly may read; readwrite may also write. A legacy admin scope exists on old keys and behaves as a superset; it is not offered to new keys.

key.description: The raw key. Returned in this response only — it is never readable again.

scan_status.description: Only `ok` is served for a code asset.

subscription_charges.description: null means charge for as long as the subscription runs.

ProductWrite.description: Product fields to create or change. On PUT, omitted fields are unchanged.

Summary.description: Workspace totals: sale counts by status, revenue net of refunds, and record counts.

info.description:
The JomForm REST API. Every route is under `/v1/rest/` and is authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`; the same key also authenticates the JomForm MCP server. Keys are created in Settings → API keys, or with `POST /v1/rest/keys`.

**Server to server only.** The API sends no `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers, so a browser page on another origin cannot read a response. This is deliberate, not an omission: the API is built for server-side calls.

**Rate limits are the exception, not the rule.** Within this API only the routes marked `x-jomform-rate-limit` are throttled; every other route has no rate limit at all. Do not build a client that assumes a uniform quota.
